description: Rust-native Minecraft world storage: content-addressed section dedup + zstd container. v0.9.55 WORST CASE: the -90% claim does not rest on untouched chunks - ALL 262144 chunks stored through the normal pipeline. v0.9.57 THE GATE CAUGHT THE CORPUS: 3 chunks whose 'edit' was canonically invisible (quantized round-reseed heights in flat zones) were caught by the CI gate and the edit was made constructive (corner block broken in every round>0 chunk). v0.9.58 THE STREAMING EXPORT: the CI runner was not flaky - the export was. export_dir materialized EVERY chunk payload (~5 GB at 262k chunks) into RAM before writing a region byte; both CI attempts of the worst-case gate died (runner shutdown, exit 143) about 2 minutes into the export phase, right after every real gate had passed (phase A x0.0588 = 241 B/chunk, lifecycle 262144 edits -> 0 pristine remain, verify bad=0 both phases, ratio B x0.0739 = 303 B/chunk). The fix groups KEYS only (~8 B each) and streams the payload of one region at a time (1024 chunks ~ 20 MB peak): same key order, same region layout, same report semantics. Local replay on a 3 GB sandbox (RAM that kills the old export): 256 regions, 262144 chunks, 1,073,741,824 B, 0 pristine_skipped, 0 lost, 146 s. 75/75 tests green.
